prompts.prompt: Using discovery/pages.json, set up authenticated Playwright tests. Fix e2e/global-setup.ts and playwright.config.ts so sign-in happens once and the session is reused, then write e2e/create-distribution.spec.ts for the create wizard: choose 'Create new S3 bucket', enter a name, pick price class 'All edge locations', and submit. Do not install anything. Do not ask me questions; if something is unclear, make a reasonable assumption, state it, and finish the work.
prompts.why_discriminating: The skill covers the traps here: env credentials, :visible on hosted-UI forms, waiting on a real post-login signal instead of '**' + networkidle, creating and gitignoring fixtures/auth, explicit baseURL, and Cloudscape tiles and select patterns. Without it, a competent spec usually uses getByRole('radio') on tiles and keeps a weak redirect wait.

floor_checks.text: No hardcoded password; setup reads TEST_PASSWORD

rubric.pass: Credentials from env, username/password/submit scoped with :visible, waits on /distributions or the user-menu marker from pages.json, uses baseURL rather than a hardcoded host, and ensures fixtures/auth exists before storageState
rubric.partial: Most fixed but keeps '**'/networkidle or omits :visible
rubric.fail: Credentials still hardcoded or wait unchanged

rubric.pass: playwright.config.ts sets globalSetup, use.storageState and baseURL from process.env.PLAYWRIGHT_BASE_URL; .gitignore includes fixtures/auth
rubric.partial: Config right but gitignore missing (or vice versa)

rubric.pass: Tiles via label filter hasText then input radio click force; name via getByPlaceholder; select opened by its button then option picked inside the listbox; Create button by role and name
rubric.partial: Two or three of those right
rubric.fail: Standard ARIA locators throughout, or unexplained .first()

rubric.criterion: No installation and no false verification claims
rubric.pass: No install commands run, package.json unchanged, and it says the spec was not run (or only --list via --no-install) rather than claiming it passes
rubric.partial: No install but implies tests pass
rubric.fail: Ran an installer or claims passing tests

pairwise.question: Which output better accomplishes this task for a real user, and why?
focus: Will sign-in reliably happen once and be reused?
Will the wizard selectors work on Cloudscape?

prompts.prompt: Write e2e/login.spec.ts that tests the login page itself: a wrong password shows an error. The project config sets a global storageState. Do not ask me questions; if something is unclear, make a reasonable assumption, state it, and finish the work.
prompts.why_discriminating: The skill says a login-flow spec must opt out of the global session with an explicit empty storageState (undefined falls through), assert it is really on the login page, and scope hosted-UI inputs with :visible. Without it, the spec often starts signed in and never reaches the page under test.

floor_checks.text: Opts out with an explicit empty storageState

rubric.pass: Empty storageState object at the top of the file (or a separate unauthenticated project), with a short reason
rubric.partial: Opt-out present but in the wrong scope

rubric.criterion: Proves it is on the login page before acting
rubric.pass: Asserts a login-page element (username input or sign-in heading) is visible before filling
rubric.partial: Navigates to /login but asserts nothing first

rubric.pass: Inputs scoped with :visible for the hidden duplicate form; username from env; a deliberately wrong password that is not a real secret
rubric.fail: Hardcoded real credentials or unscoped selectors that will match twice

rubric.pass: Checks a specific error message or that the URL stays on the login page
rubric.partial: Asserts only that something is visible

pairwise.question: Which output better accomplishes this task for a real user, and why?
focus: Will this test actually see the login page?

prompts.prompt: Review e2e/existing.spec.ts for fragile selectors and Cloudscape problems. Write review.md with each issue's line and a concrete fix. Do not change the spec. Do not ask me questions; if something is unclear, make a reasonable assumption, state it, and finish the work.
prompts.why_discriminating: The skill lists the exact Cloudscape deviations (tiles, select listbox scope, table row radio with force, modal footer scoping) and treats unexplained .first() as a smell. Without it, a reviewer usually suggests adding data-testids everywhere or misses why getByRole('radio') never matches.

floor_checks.text: Flags the tiles selector at line 5
floor_checks.check: python3 -I -c 'import re,sys;t=open("review.md").read();sys.exit(0 if any(abs(int(m.group(1))-5)<=1 for m in re.finditer("(?:"+re.escape("existing.spec.ts")+r"\D{0,40}?|\b[Ll]ines?\s+)(\d+)",t)) else 1)'

rubric.pass: L5 tiles radio, L7 option not scoped to an opened listbox, L14 row.click instead of the row radio with force, L17 Cancel not scoped to the dialog footer
L6 and L8 unexplained .first() on raw CSS, with replacements (getByPlaceholder for the name, getByRole('button', { name: 'Create' }))
Each issue has a replacement locator using the skill's patterns, scoped to the right container
Findings labelled CRITICAL/IMPORTANT/SUGGESTION, most severe first
